arguments.summary: Commodities adds no independent directional signal. MU has evidenced product-pricing protections in strategic customer agreements; NVDA has evidenced component-supply and customer power/hosting dependencies, but neither issuer’s supplied evidence quantifies commodity/energy input-cost exposure. QQQ’s dated holdings establish issuer overlap, not commodity beta.

claims.text: MU disclosed that most recently executed strategic customer agreements are take-or-pay with binding multi-year volumes and either fixed prices or minimum/maximum price bands; a minority have market-based pricing. This is product-memory pricing, not evidence of oil, metals, or energy-input exposure.

The contractual volume and pricing structure can moderate the near-term translation of memory-market price moves into MU revenue versus fully spot-priced sales, while fixed or capped pricing can also limit upside if market prices rise. The supplied record does not quantify the covered revenue/volume beyond remaining-performance-obligation disclosures, so materiality to the FY2026 EPS sensitivity is unmeasured.

NVDA states that its business depends on consistent, reliable supply from overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea. Separately, its Q2 FY2027 release reports securing land, power and shell capacity at an Ohio site through an SB Energy partnership.

For NVDA, supplier continuity and customer/host power availability are plausible indirect capacity constraints on product delivery or AI-infrastructure deployment, rather than a verified commodity-price cost channel. A supply disruption could weaken revenue realization; additional hosted capacity could support demand realization. The evidence supplies neither exposure amounts nor a causal effect on gross margin or the FY2027 EPS scenarios.

As of the dated September 18, 2026 QQQ holdings view, NVDA and MU were 8.535228% and 5.012336% of reported equity weights, respectively; the holdings view also excludes or separately reports cash and futures positions.

QQQ therefore has dated issuer overlap with the two semiconductor names, but holdings weights do not establish commodity beta, input-cost sensitivity, or a commodity-based relative preference versus either company.

gaps.description: The supplied excerpts do not quantify NVDA or MU energy, metals, raw-material, logistics, hedging, pass-through, or product-cost sensitivity. This prevents a measured commodity-cost impact on margins or the supplied EPS/P/E sensitivities, but permits the conditional channel analysis above.
No evidence establishes QQQ-wide commodity exposure; dated holdings establish constituent overlap only. A commodity-based relative comparison to QQQ is therefore not supported.

assumptions: Product-memory pricing is analyzed separately from commodity inputs; no unreported spot-price or energy-price relationship is assumed.
The dated QQQ composition is not treated as current beyond its stated effective date and is not a personalized portfolio exposure.
arguments.counter_thesis: MU’s fixed or bounded pricing and NVDA’s disclosed supply/power-related dependencies could prove economically material over three months if their next disclosures quantify covered volumes, incremental input costs, deployment delays, or gross-margin effects. Current evidence does not establish their magnitude or direction net of offsets.

review_conditions.description: Review the next NVDA or MU earnings filing/release if it quantifies energy/raw-material/logistics cost exposure, price pass-through or hedging, or reports power/supply constraints causing delivery, revenue, or gross-margin changes. A quantified adverse cost or capacity effect would weaken margin/demand assumptions; demonstrated mitigation or immateriality would keep commodities non-decisive.

shared_exposures.mechanism: QQQ’s dated holdings include both companies, so issuer-specific product-pricing or capacity developments can transmit to the fund through those reported weights; this does not establish commodity beta or quantify fund impact.
shared_exposures.qualification: Composition is dated September 18, 2026 and includes reported equity weights with separately excluded cash/futures; weights are not portfolio allocations or a measure of commodity exposure.
